metadata.geometry_method: Overpass corridor fetch per branch (all railway ways: rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled), Dijkstra over a graph in which ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q cost 1x and everything else 3x, waypoints taken from the research report's own via lists and snapped by a dynamic program over up to eight candidate nodes each, with each leg confined to a corridor around its own straight line so the router cannot wander onto a parallel railroad. Every feature's geometry_quality gives its traced length against the report's documented mileage and names any straight-line legs.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: EVERY BRANCH IN THIS FILE THAT ENDS IN 1952 HAS AN UNKNOWN, WITHHELD END YEAR. The Feb 1952 Official Guide is a single snapshot: it proves the trains were running in September 1951 and says nothing about when they stopped. The Burlington's branch passenger service was swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and NOT ONE of those discontinuances has been dated by any source consulted. A 1952 end here is where the evidence stops, not where the trains stopped -- do not 'fix' one by rounding it up. Nor is a start year the year a line opened: it is the earliest year a timetable proves, usually a branchline.uk Official-Guide snapshot letter (1875, 1884 or 1893), and the lines are older than the map shows. branchline.uk cannot close a Burlington branch, only open one: outside Nebraska's single d = 1950t there is NO lettered timetable snapshot for the CB&Q between 1893 and 1976 in any of Fowler's state files, and the Missouri CB&Q legend is blank in every position. Still unexploited, and the highest-value source left for this railroad: the 1952 Guide's index of stations carries a per-station freight-only dagger across the whole 11,000-mile system, but the OCR has mangled that dagger into at least four different characters and it was not used.

properties.line: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Chicago – Aurora (suburban)
properties.speed_source: estimated, NOT sourced: a 37.5 mi suburban run with frequent stops on a triple-track raceway; no timetable running times were consulted
properties.geometry_source: sliced from data/burlington_route_illinois.geojson (the CB&Q's own Chicago - Quincy main line) at the point nearest Aurora, 2026-08-30
properties.geometry_quality: NOT AN INDEPENDENT TRACE. The suburban service ran on the Chicago - Quincy main line's own rails, so the geometry here is the first 37.7 mi of that feature's coordinates, cut at the nearest point to Aurora. It therefore inherits that layer's geometry quality, which is a GTFS-derived alignment of the modern Amtrak route over the same physical line, not a fresh OpenStreetMap trace -- it is a coarse 135-point centreline, and this slice keeps 25 of those points over 37.7 mi. Traced 37.7 mi against a documented 37.5 mi. Good enough to show where the service ran; not good enough to read curvature off.

segments.note: The Burlington's Chicago - Aurora suburban service, the heaviest commuter operation on the system and the home of the first gallery bi-level commuter cars (1950). DRAWN FROM 1951 ONLY BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE EVIDENCE STARTS -- the CB&Q ran suburban trains out of Chicago from the 1860s, but no first-service year was established and the Guide's own suburban tables are among those the cached OCR lost, so the 19th-century decades are omitted rather than guessed. The 1970 end is the Burlington Northern merger (2 March 1970), an operator change, not the end of service: BN ran it 1970-1974 and the RTA/Metra from 1974, and it is today's Metra BNSF Line, already drawn in data/metra.geojson. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
